facts.text: McBride developed as a small rural farming community in what was then Indian Territory within the bounds of the Chickasaw Nation.
Early settlement in McBride occurred around the turn of the 20th century, spurred by the arrival of several regional railway lines.
The initial economy near McBride centered on livestock raising and cotton cultivation, leveraging the rich soils of the Red River basin.
McBride sits on flat to gently rolling plains characteristic of the Cross Timbers ecoregion in south-central Oklahoma.
Proximity to Tornado Alley exposes McBride to occasional severe weather, including tornadoes and hail, especially from March to June.
Archaeological evidence in the McBride area points to prehistoric habitation dating back to the Paleo-Indian and Woodland periods.
